The protocol horizon is positive and interval endpoints satisfy the ordered nonempty-interval inequalities. At a single round the path-length increment sum is empty and equals zero, leaving the declared leading unit; the comparator action set is nonempty by the inherited protocol.

The detected phrase exactly when is the definiteness axiom of the norm supplied as input. It is not a theorem characterizing regret or strongly adaptive algorithms, so there is no separate forward regret implication to prove.

The norm input already requires that only the zero vector has zero norm. The item then defines loss differences and a one-way strongly-adaptive bound; it does not assert a converse performance characterization.

The reward sums run over positive horizon and positive arm cardinality. Empty individual arm events have probability zero and contribute zero through the finite partition calculation; they do not require conditioning by a zero-probability event.

The expert and round cardinalities are explicitly positive integers. Consequently the positive-weight sum cannot be empty or vanish; even the singleton-expert case has one positive weight and is treated separately without dividing by a zero tuned learning rate.

The feasible set is assumed nonempty and contains the supplied initial iterate; each comparator is also in that set. Horizon and ambient dimension are positive. The zero-diameter branch still has a singleton feasible set, not an empty projection domain.

The number of probability coordinates is at least two, and the uniform distribution supplies a point in the simplex interior. The finite entropy sum and independent-coordinate domain are therefore nonempty; zero coordinates at vertices are covered by the separate continuity convention.

The time index and ambient dimension are inherited from the AdaGrad procedure and its positive rounds. Even if an initial empty accumulated Gram sum were considered, its entries and nonnegative square roots would be zero; the displayed positive-round identity introduces no empty maximum or division.

The Statement supplies an initial point in the nonempty feasible intersection and assumes a positive round count. Every projected iterate is expressly assumed to exist in that intersection, so the finite regret and local-norm sums do not conceal an empty projection domain.

The refuted Statement requires a nonempty decision set with nonempty interior and a positive horizon. The admissible witness uses a genuine closed interval and one round, so the detected regret sum never ranges over an empty set.
The Statement requires integer n at least five, so the summation from one through n minus one is nonempty; the detector sees a finite aggregate but no empty-domain case is admitted.
The Statement explicitly requires a positive scale a, while the other symbolic denominator one plus a real square is everywhere positive. Neither denominator can vanish on the claimed domain.
